title: Using Drosophila melanogaster Larvae to Model Human Glioblastoma
author: Saborio, Young, et al.

steps.title: Retrieve brains from cold storage
steps.instruction: Remove dissected larval brains from 4 °C storage and peel off the transparent tape covering the wells.

steps.title: Aspirate PBS and add blocking solution
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, aspirate the 1× PBS 0.3 % Triton sodium azide solution from each well, then add 100 µL of blocking solution consisting of 1× PBS, 0.3 % Triton, 10 % normal goat serum (NGS), and 0.1 % sodium azide; incubate for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Add primary antibody and seal
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL of primary antibody solution (e.g., anti‑Repo at 1:10 dilution from the Developmental Studies Hybridoma Bank) ensuring the brains are fully submerged, cover the wells with transparent tape to create an airtight seal, and incubate at 4 °C for 48 h (48–72 h acceptable).

steps.title: Remove primary antibody and wash
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove the tape, aspirate the primary antibody solution (which may be stored at 4 °C for reuse), then wash the brains three times with 100 µL of 1× PBS 0.3 % Triton for 10 min each (total 30 min).

steps.title: Add secondary antibody and seal
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL of secondary antibody solution containing F(ab’)₂ fragments (optionally include a fluorescent anti‑HRP for neuronal counterstaining), ensure complete submersion, tape the wells airtight, and store at 4 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Remove secondary antibody and wash
steps.instruction: Remove the tape, aspirate the secondary antibody solution, then wash three times with 100 µL of 1× PBS 0.3 % Triton for 10 min each (total 30 min).

steps.title: Mount brains in antifade medium
steps.instruction: Aspirate the final wash, resuspend the brains in Vectashield antifade mounting medium (with DAPI if desired, otherwise without), cover the wells with tape, and store at 4 °C for 24 h to allow clearing; brains can be kept in Vectashield at 4 °C for 3–6 months.

steps.title: Capture low‑magnification z‑stacks
steps.instruction: Image whole larval brains at low magnification (≈10×) using a Zeiss LSM confocal to obtain .czi z‑stack files.

steps.title: Quantify brain volume in Imaris
steps.instruction: Import the .czi files into Imaris, select brain hemispheres (exclude ventral nerve cord) using the draw tool every 2–3 slices, and let Imaris calculate the 3‑D volume in mm³ for each brain.

steps.title: Normalize volumes and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Measure 10–20 brains per experimental and control group, normalize each brain’s volume to the average control volume, then analyze the normalized data with an unpaired t‑test for pairwise comparisons or two‑way ANOVA for multiple groups.

steps.title: Capture high‑magnification images
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑magnification (≈40×) images of representative brain regions, matched for section plane, for both experimental and control samples.

steps.title: Create projections and count glia
steps.instruction: Generate 3 µm‑thick optical projections from at least five age‑matched brains per genotype, view only the Repo fluorescence channel, and manually count Repo‑positive nuclei using Zen, ImageJ, or Photoshop.

steps.title: Analyze glial counts statistically
steps.instruction: Report total glial cells per brain hemisphere per projection; use data from ≥5 animals per genotype and apply unpaired t‑tests for pairwise comparisons or two‑way ANOVA for multiple comparisons.
